title: Search Products by Name
description: Find the products with "pro" anywhere in their name, in any case, using LIKE.
statement:
Return the `name` and `category` of every product whose name **contains** the letters `pro`, anywhere in the name and in any mix of capital and small letters (`Pro Keyboard`, `Improved Chair` and `PROTEIN Bar` all match).

Sort by `name`.
variants: INSERT INTO products VALUES (103, 'Improved Chair', 'home', 80.0), (104, 'PROTEIN Bar', 'home', 3.0)
hints: Which operator compares text to a pattern instead of to a whole value?
The pattern needs a wildcard on each side of the word.
The other data has names with `pro` in the middle and in capitals: SQLite's `LIKE` already ignores case.
solution:
SELECT name, category
FROM products
WHERE name LIKE '%pro%'
ORDER BY name;
explanation:
**The idea.** `LIKE` matches a pattern: `%` stands for any number of characters (including none) and `_` for exactly one. Putting `%` on both sides finds the text anywhere in the value. In SQLite `LIKE` ignores the case of ASCII letters; other databases differ (PostgreSQL has `ILIKE` for that).

**Usual mistakes.** `LIKE 'pro%'` only finds names that start with it; `=` compares the whole value; searching with a leading `%` cannot use an ordinary index, so on a big table it reads every row (full-text search or a trigram index is the fix).
